what_it_does.name: firecrawl
what_it_does.summary: Instructions for doing live-web tasks through the Firecrawl CLI. It searches the web, scrapes static and JS-rendered pages, maps and crawls sites, interacts with pages through clicks, forms and login, downloads sites and sets monitors for changes, and returns clean markdown optimized for LLM context windows. Results are written to files in .firecrawl/ and read in bounded parts. Use it for ordinary web research and content gathering, web only, with local files going to firecrawl-parse.
tasks: search the web and gather sources
scrape a page or a list of known URLs
map a site to find a subpage and crawl a site section
interact with a page through clicks, form fills, pagination or login
download a site to local files
watch pages for changes with a monitor
find US law or regulation with gov search

outputs.what: search results, with page content when scraped

outputs.form: markdown file, or JSON for several formats
outputs.destination: .firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md, or the agent's context when the user asks for it

outputs.what: auth state, concurrency limit, remaining credits and credit usage
a monitor that runs recurring scrapes or crawls and alerts on changes
outputs.destination: the Firecrawl account, with alerts by webhook or email

outputs.what: clicks, form submissions and multi-step navigation on a page
feedback on a search or a job

inputs.type: a quoted URL in a command
inputs.for: scraping, mapping, crawling and interacting with a known page or site
running a structured-data tool found by search

inputs.what: a jurisdiction and date for a legal question

when_input_is_missing.case: a legal question names no jurisdiction
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: the agent asks for the jurisdiction before identifying the governing rule
search, scrape and interact run on the keyless free tier, and crawl, map, download, agent, monitor, credit-usage and feedback prompt an interactive login
the agent asks the user to log in with the browser or enter an API key

when_input_is_missing.case: an Unauthorized: Invalid token or insufficient-credits error
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: the agent checks firecrawl --status once, reports the blocking reason and stops

exclusions: not for local files, which route to firecrawl-parse
not for research papers, which go to firecrawl-research-index
not for library, API, error or bug questions, which go to firecrawl-developer-index
not for tasks needing capabilities Firecrawl lacks
not for integrating Firecrawl into an app, which goes to the firecrawl-build skills

reading output files in bounded parts and working with JSON output
running firecrawl and npx firecrawl-cli commands

checks.tool: Snyk, skills.sh audit, version not stated
checks.result: warn, risk level MEDIUM, 1 issue, W011 third-party content exposure, indirect prompt injection risk, scored low risk 0.10

checks.tool: Gen Agent Trust Hub, skills.sh audit, version not stated
checks.scope: SKILL.md, rules/install.md and rules/security.md, as cited in its analysis
checks.result: pass, risk level SAFE, three categories described, indirect prompt injection, external downloads through npm and npx, and command execution through Bash

checks.tool: Socket, skills.sh audit, version not stated
checks.result: pass, checks for malicious behaviour, security concerns, code obfuscation and suspicious patterns

vulnerabilities.finding: Third-party content exposure, indirect prompt injection risk, W011

risks.risk: Instructions hidden in fetched web pages reach the agent, since search, scrape, crawl and map bring outsider-authored text into its context.
risks.severity: MEDIUM by C1, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: in place as instructions, output isolated in .firecrawl/, read in bounded parts, and instructions in page content not followed

risks.risk: An unquoted URL in a shell command can lead to command injection.
risks.mitigation: in place as an instruction to always quote URLs

risks.risk: Installing with npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest or npm install -g runs whatever version npm serves at that time with the user's privileges.
risks.mitigation: none stated, C2 notes the package comes from the official vendor

risks.risk: Clicks, form fills and logins through interact can submit data or change accounts on third-party websites.
An API key passed with firecrawl login --api-key stays in shell history or logs.
risks.mitigation: none stated, browser login is the recommended path

limitations: Gov search filters keep only pages the index has labeled, so a filtered search can leave out relevant pages.
Gov results are excerpts, not a guarantee of official-only sources or current governing law, and no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists.
The keyless free tier is rate-limited, and crawl, map, download, agent, monitor, credit-usage and the feedback commands need an account.
The client cannot be assumed to signal an overflow back to the tool, and Bash cannot be assumed to support search IDs or every provider's retained data.
search --categories research is a website filter, not the paper index.

known_problems.problem: Unauthorized: Invalid token or insufficient-credits error
known_problems.workaround: verify config once with firecrawl --status, report the blocking reason and stop, since retrying yields the same error
log in with firecrawl login --browser or firecrawl login --api-key

known_problems.problem: firecrawl is not found after installation
known_problems.workaround: put the npm global bin in PATH, try npx firecrawl-cli@latest --version, or reinstall

known_problems.problem: the CLI is missing, stale or only partially configured
a client context or output error
known_problems.workaround: keep the request or scrape ID and inspect saved output or use scrape firecrawl/bash before repeating the request
